hook: this is the pipe layer from briefing #20's whitespace becoming a live product.
market_map: Today's stories: The biggest MLS in the US just went live with single-entry listings; REdistribute opens direct broker licensing; FBS ships Flexmls Scout; RealReports lands a second Texas MLS.
where_we_play: Bright × Ocusell is live at the largest MLS with OneList as the national pitch; ORE runs its vendor RFP through Q1 2027. Whoever wins the entry layer sets the standard for how listings get entered, checked, and distributed — and the loser still has 30 MLSs of distribution. The opening that survives either outcome is the broker-side comparison: which entry pipe, what it costs per listing, what data rights you keep, what happens if you leave. It needs no MLS credentialing to prototype (it tracks deals and destinations, not listings), and every new pipe — Ocusell, ORE, HouseCanary's Google pipe — makes it more valuable. Second thread, from finding 2: the institutional licensing model is proven; the agent-facing licensed-data product on the same terms is still unbuilt.
one_line: The vendor-pick race is now a two-horse story with a deadline.

stories.title: The biggest MLS in the US just went live with single-entry listings — Ocusell, plus a new OneList platform (Nov 3, catch-up missed by #20)
stories.summary: Bright MLS — the nation's largest MLS, 100,000+ professionals across the Mid-Atlantic — and Ocusell activated their live integration: brokers and agents operating across markets can now create and edit a listing once in Ocusell and push compliance-checked data directly into Bright and their other destination MLSs. this is the pipe layer from briefing #20's whitespace becoming a live product. Flag: vendor release (GlobeNewswire). Performance figures are Ocusell's own. Released Nov 3, 1:16 PM PT — inside #20's window but after its morning sweep; filed here as a catch-up, not as Nov 5 news.

stories.title: REdistribute opens direct broker licensing — the "who gets paid for listing data" question already has a working answer (Nov 4, catch-up)
stories.summary: REdistribute — the MLS-owned joint venture (founded 2022 by Bright MLS and California Regional MLS, investors include BeachesMLS, REcolorado, Stellar MLS, MLS PIN, MARIS) that licenses MLS listing data for institutional use — will now partner directly with brokerages to fill coverage gaps in markets where the local MLS has not joined. this is the closest thing in this record to a proven answer to Jessica's core question — can listing data be licensed on terms that pay the people who create it? Flag: vendor release (GlobeNewswire, Nov 4, 6:58 AM PT — just before #20 filed; missed by its sweep). Coverage percentages and the compensation framing are the company's own. No pricing disclosed. REdistribute's Chris Bennett will be at NAR NXT in New Orleans, Nov 6–8, meeting MLS leaders and brokers — watch for positioning news out of that event.

stories.title: FBS ships Flexmls Scout — an AI assistant inside the MLS, with the permissions built in (Nov 5)
stories.summary: FBS introduced Flexmls Scout, an AI assistant built into its Flexmls platform: agents search MLS data, review market activity, and get business insights through plain-language prompts — search listings, pull market statistics and contact/production details, generate comparative market analyses, and ask questions about MLS rules and policies without leaving the platform. this is the sanctioned-AI template from briefing #5 (Cotality Trestle MCP + Defender) and the spring FlexMLS MCP server, now with a native assistant on top. Flag: vendor announcement via trade-press roundup; no adoption, accuracy, or pricing figures. Scout is an enterprise add-on for Flexmls MLS customers, not a standalone consumer product.

stories.title: RealReports lands a second Texas MLS — the MLS-funded AI prospecting wave keeps spreading (Nov 4)
stories.summary: LERA MLS is giving more than 15,000 members across San Antonio and South Texas access to RealReports, the property-intelligence platform, effective immediately. the product shape is familiar — past-client data plus public records plus an agent's own inbox, ranked into daily prospecting. Flag: vendor announcement via Inman roundup. Property-count figures are the company's own; no pricing or adoption figures for LERA members.

watch.title: Tuccori/NAR buyer settlement: STILL no outcome surfaced, three days after the Nov 2 final approval hearing.
watch.text: Checked again this morning: the freshest tracker update found (Lawfold, updated Nov 1) still describes the hearing as set for Nov 2; no order, ruling, or reputable report of an outcome has surfaced. The judge may have taken the matter under advisement, or an order may not yet be posted — either way, do not cite approval until an order or a reputable report lands. Fund $120,334,500, NAR share $52.25M; claims closed Oct 27; no payment date until approval. Source: https://lawfold.com/nar-lawsuit/

watch.title: Compass cooperation-rules fight: no new filing or ruling in-window.
watch.text: Nov 3–4 recaps (NY Post, The Real Deal, The Mortgage Point) restate the known picture: six regional MLSs in the October suit, OneKey MLS joining the CRMLS suit, ~272,000 subscribers behind the MLS side. Next event is still Compass's anticipated motion to dismiss, with no trial date set in either SDNY case. No SFARMLS position has surfaced either way.

watch.title: NAR NXT, Nov 6–8, New Orleans:
watch.text: the industry's big annual event starts tomorrow. REdistribute is holding MLS/broker meetings there; watch for ORE positioning, MLS AI announcements, and any Tuccori-adjacent commentary.

watch.title: No new movement in-window on:
watch.text: NAR rule changes; FTC or state enforcement actions affecting agent tools or listing-data use; RESO MCP Profile adoption; SFARMLS data-access news.

watch.title: Standing, unchanged:
watch.text: NAR's Clear Cooperation Policy still being defended on multiple fronts; CVR MLS AI-access ban (effective Oct 1) still the only named MLS AI ban in this record; NAR broker AI rulebook (briefing #13) still the clearest gray-zone line; state private-listing laws keep spreading (WA June, CT Oct 1, WI Jan 1 2027, NY awaiting signature); Cotality Trestle MCP + Defender (briefing #5) still the sanctioned-AI template; RESO Web API remains the standard, and each MLS's vendor credentialing remains the gate.
